title: Audit the fixed substitution projection of Cheshire’s published method
statement: Cheshire (2019), University of Bristol accepted author manuscript and appended Method Paper, https://research-information.bris.ac.uk/ws/files/201563069/Full_text_PDF_accepted_author_manuscript_.pdf. The main article describes two a forms that usually vary by word position and also lists exceptions (figs. 1–4). The appended Figure 12 (PDF p. 48) gives 28 entries in two columns of 14. Five entries list explicit alternatives apart from doubled-letter spellings: two list s/z, one sa/za, one v/f/fv/ph/pv, and the ae ligature lists four alternatives beside the main value. The appended f53 worked example then uses a priority order across languages, alternate spellings and abbreviations, and chooses word divisions and reorders words when interpreting sentences. Its first line glosses la using Italian, French or Ladin and ona using Galician or Basque, while other items are glossed through Latin. I could identify a concrete alphabet projection to test, but the published procedure also needs rules for selecting alternative outputs, choosing boundaries and inserting connective words. A fixed key into a single reference language measures one set of glyph correspondences. The additional decisions require a separate test. The published method's mixed target has no independent matching corpus on the record.
check: For K-016-open-1, freeze a Figure 12 crosswalk to one named transliteration and declare how each optional output and multi-glyph sign is handled before evaluation. Verify against the printed italic transcription of the f53 example before scoring. State the language and period of each proxy separately, with the same decoys. A test of the full procedure separately requires deterministic, predeclared rules for segmentation, choosing lexical alternatives and evaluating the resulting mixed-language text.
